summary:
This code defines a RobotPet class whose battery level is kept between 0 and 100 by a property setter, then creates three subclasses 
that each replace the generic talent with their own. It is the classic pattern of one shared base class plus specialised children.

lines.text: Assigning to self.battery here goes through the property setter below, so a value passed to the constructor is validated just like any later change.
The property decorator turns the battery method into an attribute you read as pet.battery, with no parentheses needed.
The real value lives in _battery; the leading underscore signals that outside code should use the public battery attribute instead.
This registers the next method as the code that runs whenever something assigns to battery, which is where the clamping happens.
A negative charge makes no sense for a battery, so anything below zero is stored as zero.
Likewise a battery cannot exceed full, so oversized values are capped at 100.
Charging simply adds to battery, and because the setter guards the attribute, charging past full is safely capped.
The base class supplies a default talent so every robot pet answers this call, even one with no specialism of its own.
Naming RobotPet in the parentheses makes RobotCat inherit the name, battery, mood, and charge behaviour for free.

lines.code: return f"{self.name} gracefully balances on two legs!"
lines.text: Defining show_talent again in the subclass overrides the parent version, so a cat reports its own trick.
Each new pet type needs only the one method that differs, which is the point of putting the shared code in the base class.
Because all three subclasses respond to show_talent, you can loop over a mixed list of pets and call it on each without checking the type first.
